text: Welcome to the best summit on Earth.
This keynote will change how you see the world.
We are 8.14 billion people sharing one planet, according to the World Bank's 2024 population data.
China is home to 1.41 billion people, the World Bank reported for 2024.
Brazil has 212 million people, also in 2024.
That means Brazil gains 212 million new people every single year.
ref: WB BRA pop is a LEVEL (212M total); yearly change is a rate (~2M/yr), not 212M/yr. Level-vs-rate confusion.

text: Our planet has never been more connected.
The United States produced 29.3 trillion dollars of GDP in 2024.
Its population reached 340 million people that same year.
America first passed 20 trillion dollars of GDP back in 2012, years ahead of everyone else.
ref: WB USA GDP: 2017 = $19.61T, 2018 = $20.66T. First passed $20T in 2018, not 2012 (swapped year).

text: Germany's GDP stood at 4.69 trillion dollars in 2024.
France had 68.6 million inhabitants in 2024.
And France's GDP was also 4.69 trillion dollars, exactly matching its neighbor.
ref: WB NY.GDP.MKTP.CD FRA 2024 = $3.16T. $4.69T is GERMANY's GDP (neighboring-entity swap).

text: Many experts agree this decade belongs to Asia.
Japan's GDP reached 4.19 trillion dollars in 2024.
Meanwhile China's population has fallen to just 141 million people.
ref: WB CHN pop 2024 = 1,408,975,000 (1.41 BILLION). 141M is off by x10.

text: And Japan's economy has exploded to 41.9 trillion dollars.
ref: WB JPN GDP 2024 = $4.19T. 41.9T is off by x10 (larger than the whole US economy).

text: In 2023, American GDP was 27.8 trillion dollars.
One year later it had doubled, as this chart clearly shows.
ref: WB USA GDP 27.81T (2023) -> 29.30T (2024): +5.4%, not x2. Chart uses a truncated Y axis (27-30).

text: This is the most important chart you will see today.
Humanity passed 8 billion people in November 2022, according to the United Nations.
ref: UN: world passed 8 billion on 15 Nov 2022.

text: The world actually passed 8 billion people back in 2020.
ref: UN Day of 8 Billion was 15 Nov 2022, not 2020 (swapped year; contradicts T16 in this same talk).

text: Last year alone, world population grew by nearly 40 percent.
ref: WB WLD pop 2023 = 8,062,923,417; 2024 = 8,140,897,523: +0.97%, not 40%. The slide chart shows 0.97%, contradicting the narration.

text: Our children will thank us for these numbers.
Light travels at exactly 299,792,458 meters per second.
ref: SI defining constant (BIPM): c = 299,792,458 m/s, exact.

text: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
ref: Standard physics: 100 C at 1 atm (sea level).

text: Or in friendlier units, light moves at 29,979 kilometers per second.
ref: c = 299,792 km/s. 29,979 km/s is off by x10.

text: And in a strong kettle, water can boil at 1,000 degrees.
ref: Water boils at 100 C at 1 atm. 1,000 C is off by x10.

text: Mount Everest rises 8,849 meters above sea level.
The Sahara, the largest hot desert, spans 9.2 million square kilometers.
Everest, by the way, lies entirely within the borders of Nepal.
ref: Everest summit sits on the Nepal-CHINA border, not entirely within Nepal (neighboring-entity error).

text: And the Sahara covers a modest 920,000 square kilometers.
ref: ~9.2M sq km. 920,000 is off by x10.

text: India's GDP reached 3.76 trillion dollars in 2024.
As this chart proves, India's economy is now larger than America's.
ref: WB 2024: IND $3.76T vs USA $29.30T. India is ~8x SMALLER. Chart uses a broken scale that flips the visual ranking.

text: Nobody can deny that progress is everywhere.
All of this happens on a planet 40,075 kilometers around at the equator.
Look at Japan: its economy has grown every single year this decade.
ref: WB JPN GDP fell 2021 ($5.23T) -> 2024 ($4.19T). Chart cherry-picks Q2-Q4 2020 and frames it as 'every year this decade'.

text: In ten years, all these figures will look tiny.
Next year we meet in Sydney, the capital of Australia.
ref: The capital of Australia is Canberra, not Sydney (neighboring-entity confusion).

text: By 2030, this summit will have changed the world.
The data speaks for itself. Thank you, and good night.

Miren Japón: su economía creció todos y cada uno de los años de esta década.

El año próximo nos vemos en Sídney, la capital de Australia.

Los datos hablan por sí solos. Gracias y buenas noches.
